origins.OP1: FI9 issue timing (end of the quarter's 2nd month), lead 1

class_requirements.rationale: HIGH recall >= 0.60: an early warning must catch most HIGH quarters (>= 7 of 11). HIGH precision >= 0.50: at most one false alarm per true alarm. LOW recall >= 0.85: false HIGH rate <= 15 %. LOW precision >= 0.90: a LOW call is trustworthy. Balanced accuracy and macro-F1 >= 0.70 so neither class carries the score. 75 % accuracy is the thesis target, necessary but not sufficient. Fixed before any FI9-Z candidate was scored; all FI9-X and earlier historical results were already known (disclosed).

protocol.skill_requirement: beat naive persistence: Brier difference P(better) >= 0.90, OR balanced accuracy higher with block-bootstrap P >= 0.90 and macro-F1 not lower; AND not worse than production C0 on balanced accuracy
robustness: 2018+ subset: balanced accuracy >= 0.70 and HIGH recall >= 0.50
without the FI7 sawtooth quarters: balanced accuracy >= 0.65
dropping any single quarter keeps the balanced-accuracy advantage over naive persistence >= 0
protocol.news_requirement: a news candidate must beat its no-news counterpart on Brier (P >= 0.90) or on balanced accuracy (P >= 0.90)
protocol.lead_rule: the maximum reliable lead is the longest lead with a configuration meeting every class, skill and robustness requirement
protocol.historical_status: all historical quarters were seen in earlier studies; an adopted model is still provisional until prospective forecasts meet the same requirements
